artiest/thomas-anders.text:
Thomas Anders, born Bernd Weidung in 1963 in Koblenz, is a German singer, songwriter and producer. He grew up in the village of Mörz and performed as a child under the name Bernie von der Mosel. After finishing school he studied musicology in Mainz, intending to become a music journalist. At the start of his career he spent years trying his luck as a schlager singer under the stage name Thomas Anders, but his first singles on CBS and Hansa failed to chart. In 1983 he met the producer Dieter Bohlen.

Together they formed the Eurodisco duo Modern Talking. Their breakthrough came in 1985, when the video for You're My Heart, You're My Soul was shown on the German music programme Formel Eins. The song reached the top ten in thirty-five countries and spent six weeks at number one in Germany. It was followed by You Can Win If You Want, Cheri, Cheri Lady, Brother Louie and Atlantis Is Calling, all of them number ones in Germany. The music was simple and catchy, with English lyrics, a high falsetto voice and plain rhythms. In 1987 the duo split after a quarrel. They reunited in 1998 and continued until 2003. By their own account they sold 120 million records together.

His solo career in the 1990s was not very successful, apart from the Spanish-language Barcos de Cristal in 1994 in Argentina. After 2003 things went better, with This Time in 2004 and the German-language Pures Leben in 2017. In Eastern Europe he is regarded as a musical icon, and according to the source he is the best-selling foreign artist in Russia.
artiest/thomas-anders.listen: Listen to You're My Heart, You're My Soul and notice Thomas Anders's high falsetto above the simple, unbroken rhythm. Can you hear how few chords it takes to make a hit?

artiest/thomas-bangalter.text:
Thomas Bangalter, born in Paris in 1975, is a French musician, producer, DJ and composer. He is best known as one half of the electronic duo Daft Punk, together with Guy-Manuel de Homem-Christo, whom he met at school in 1987. His mother was a dancer and choreographer; his father, Daniel Vangarde, wrote and produced disco for artists including the Gibson Brothers and Ottawan. Bangalter played piano as a child. With Homem-Christo and Laurent Brancowitz he first started a small indie rock band, Darlin'. A bad review described their sound as a daft punky thrash, and that became the duo's name.

Daft Punk chose electronic music. Bangalter recorded Homework in his bedroom, and his label Roulé released his own records and those of others. With Alan Braxe and Benjamin Diamond he made the club hit Music Sounds Better with You in 1998 as Stardust. He also worked with the DJ Falcon as Together. In the years that followed, Daft Punk released Discovery, Human After All and Random Access Memories, and in 2016 produced two tracks for The Weeknd. In 2002 Bangalter composed the music for the film Irréversible.

In 2021 Daft Punk split up. Bangalter then made ballet and film music on his own label, Alberts and Gothmaan, for example Mythologies in 2022 and the album Mythologies in 2023, and later Chiroptera. He gave up the robot mask because in 2023 he no longer wanted to be a robot, and said that he would not leave drum machines and synthesizers behind for good. His work has influenced a wide range of artists.
artiest/thomas-bangalter.listen: Listen to Music Sounds Better with You by Stardust and notice the filtered disco sample that keeps repeating and slowly blossoms open. Can you hear how a single loop carries the whole record?

artiest/thomas-bergersen.text:
Thomas Jacob Bergersen was born in 1980 in Trondheim, Norway, and is a Norwegian composer, multi-instrumentalist and co-founder of the production company Two Steps From Hell. He is self-taught. He began playing piano at the age of six, and as a teenager was already writing symphonic music. He made his first music as a demoscener under the name Lioz, using tracker modules. In 2009 he moved to the United States. His work is best known from film trailers and is associated with films such as Avatar, Pirates of the Caribbean and Harry Potter.

With Nick Phoenix he released the first public Two Steps From Hell album, Invincible, in 2010. Archangel and SkyWorld, among others, followed. As a solo artist he made Illusions in 2011 and Sun in 2014, and later American Dream in 2018, Seven in 2019 and Catch Me in 2020. In 2020 he began the Humanity series, a planned set of seven albums about every aspect of human emotion, the first chapter of which appeared on 1 July 2020. With singles such as Heart and The Hero in Your Heart he raised money for the victims of the Tōhoku earthquake and of Typhoon Haiyan.

Bergersen names Gustav Mahler as one of his most important influences, alongside a very wide range of musicians, and he does not care for musical genres. Many of his sounds are recorded himself, from orchestras and world instruments. He often thinks up melodies first at the grand piano. He belongs to the world of classical crossover, and Two Steps From Hell has toured with an orchestra and choir since 2022.
artiest/thomas-bergersen.listen: Listen to a track from Sun or Illusions and notice how the orchestra and choir swell in waves. Can you hear how the music works almost like a film image, with a clear build towards a climax?

artiest/thomas-dorsey.text:
Thomas Andrew Dorsey was an American musician, composer and church evangelist, born in 1899 in Villa Rica, Georgia, and died in 1993. As a boy he played blues on piano at parties and in barrelhouses in Atlanta, and in 1919 he moved to Chicago. There he wrote blues, worked as an arranger for Paramount and, as a pianist, led Ma Rainey's band. Under the name Georgia Tom he recorded the successful It's Tight Like That together with the guitarist Tampa Red. In total Dorsey wrote some three thousand songs, a third of them gospel.

After a long depression in the 1920s he chose religious music. For fifty years he was music director of the Pilgrim Baptist Church in Chicago, and he brought improvisation, clapping and call-and-response into the church, even though this was often disapproved of. In 1932 he co-founded a national association of gospel choirs, which still exists. After the death of his wife and son he wrote Take My Hand, Precious Lord. Peace in the Valley is also his. Together with Sallie Martin he started the first Black gospel publishing house.

His music fused the joy of the gospel with the sound of the blues. Apart from the lyrics, he saw little difference between blues and church music. Singers such as Mahalia Jackson, Sallie Martin and Roberta Martin and the singer James Cleveland worked or studied with him. He is called the Father of Gospel Music, although above all he set in motion a movement that made gospel blues known in Black churches and thereby also influenced American music in general.
artiest/thomas-dorsey.listen: Listen to Peace in the Valley and notice the calm, relaxed melody and the blues in the way the words are shaped. Can you hear how the singer stretches and ornaments the notes?

artiest/thomas-mapfumo.text:
Thomas Mapfumo is a Zimbabwean musician, born in 1945 in Marondera, then still in Southern Rhodesia, which was under British rule. Until the age of ten he grew up in a traditional Shona way of life in the countryside, and then moved with his family to the township of Mbare near Harare. There he came to know the traditional music of the Shona, with the ngoma drum and the mbira, an instrument with metal tongues that has a spiritual significance. At sixteen he sang in his first band. Later he played with, among others, Oliver Mtukudzi.

Mapfumo brought traditional Shona music into pop and sang in his own language. In a country governed by a white minority, that was already a political statement. His lyrics became openly political and supported the rural uprising. The style is called chimurenga. His song Hokoyo!, which means Watch out!, was banned from state radio, and in 1979 he was put in a prison camp without being charged. After the elections of 1980 he performed at a celebration concert, together with Bob Marley. Later he criticised the Mugabe government and lived for twenty years in exile in the United States. In 2018 he returned for a concert. His albums include Hokoyo! from 1978, Ndangariro from 1983 and Rise Up from 2006.

Mapfumo has influenced Zimbabwean musicians such as the Bhundu Boys and Stella Chiweshe. He shows how popular music can become the voice of a people.
artiest/thomas-mapfumo.listen: Listen to Ndanzwa Ngoma Kurira and notice the guitars, which play a pattern reminiscent of an mbira. Can you hear how the rhythms keep returning and how the vocals lie on top of them?

artiest/thomas-mars.text:
Thomas Pablo Croquet, known as Thomas Mars, was born in 1976 in Versailles and is a French musician, the singer of the indie pop band Phoenix. His uncle Horst pushed him to learn English. With school friends Chris Mazzalai and Deck d'Arcy he formed Phoenix in 1995, later joined by Laurent Brancowitz, Mazzalai's older brother, after the end of Darlin'. Mars lasted only four days at university, where he was studying economics, and then committed himself entirely to music. The band members adopted stage names to sound cooler.

The group first pressed five hundred copies of a single on their own label, before signing with the Paris-based Source Records. Mars wrote and produced Too Young, their first single in the French charts. The debut album United appeared in 2000. Phoenix released seven albums in total and won a Grammy in 2010. Under the pseudonym Gordon Tracks, Mars co-wrote Air's song Playground Love, for the film The Virgin Suicides, and also sang and played drums on it.

On that film he met the director Sofia Coppola, whom he married in 2011. They have two daughters. Mars has lived in New York since 2018, but also has a home in Paris. His work links him with the French pop wave of around 2000, to which Air and Daft Punk also belong.
artiest/thomas-mars.listen: Listen to Playground Love by Air and notice the soft, airy vocals and the floating electronic sound. Can you hear how the voice works like an extra instrument?

artiest/thomas-newman.text: Thomas Newman was born in 1955, the son of the film composer Alfred Newman. He studied at Yale. His style differs greatly from his father's. He builds music from small, repeating patterns on piano, marimba, tabla, hammered dulcimer and electronics, often using unusual playing techniques. In The Shawshank Redemption (1994) he also uses warm strings to evoke the prisoners' hope. The piano theme with percussion from American Beauty (1999) was imitated endlessly. For Pixar he wrote Finding Nemo (2003) and WALL-E (2008). His sound is also recognisable in the Bond film Skyfall (2012) and the war film 1917 (2019). He has been nominated for an Oscar many times.
artiest/thomas-newman.listen: Notice the small, rhythmic patterns of marimba, piano and percussion that together form a single moving fabric of sound.

artiest/three-6-mafia.text:
Three 6 Mafia is an American hip-hop group from Memphis, Tennessee, formed in 1991. It began as an underground horrorcore group and later broke through to the mainstream. The founders were DJ Paul, his half-brother Lord Infamous and Juicy J. At first they worked under names such as Da Serial Killaz and The Backyard Posse. In 1995 Crunchy Black and Gangsta Boo joined, and the group took the name Three 6 Mafia. The debut album Mystic Stylez, released that year, became an influential cult classic.

In 1997 DJ Paul and Juicy J founded the label Hypnotize Minds. They signed with Sony and released Chapter 2: World Domination, the first album to receive an official certification. In 1999 a subgroup made one of the first records in the crunk style. In 2000 came When the Smoke Clears: Sixty 6, Sixty 1, featuring Sippin' on Some Syrup with UGK. In 2005 Most Known Unknown arrived, with Stay Fly. In 2006 the group won an Oscar for Best Original Song, It's Hard out Here for a Pimp, from the film Hustle & Flow.

Three 6 Mafia shows how hip-hop from Memphis made its way into the mainstream. The group brought crunk and a raw Memphis sound to a large audience. For the chapter on hip-hop in the 2000s, it is a clear example of how a local scene could break through nationwide.
artiest/three-6-mafia.listen: Listen to Stay Fly and notice the chorus and the beat. Can you hear how the rappers take turns and how the rhythm builds around a simple, repeated motif?

artiest/throbbing-gristle.text:
Throbbing Gristle was an English music and visual art group, formed in Kingston upon Hull around Genesis P-Orridge and Cosey Fanni Tutti, later joined by Peter Sleazy Christopherson and Chris Carter. The group grew out of the performance art collective COUM Transmissions and made its debut in October 1976 at the exhibition Prostitution at the Institute of Contemporary Arts in London. The name is Yorkshire slang for a male erection. A British Member of Parliament consequently called the group wreckers of civilisation.

In 1977 came the single United and the album The Second Annual Report, on their own label Industrial Records. D.o.A: The Third and Final Report followed in 1978 and 20 Jazz Funk Greats in 1979. The group used recorded tapes and self-built or modified effects units to create a distorted sound, with spoken word and lyrics about mysticism, extreme politics, sex and the dark sides of society. Their image was deliberately shocking, with pornography and fascist symbolism. The group said it did not want to make attractive music, but to explore the dark and obsessive sides of human beings.

In 1981 the group split, and its members went on with Psychic TV, Coil and Chris and Cosey. In 2004 it returned, until P-Orridge left in 2010 and Christopherson died. Throbbing Gristle is regarded as one of the creators of industrial, alongside Cabaret Voltaire. The slogan industrial music for industrial people appears on The Second Annual Report.
artiest/throbbing-gristle.listen: Listen to a track from 20 Jazz Funk Greats and notice the contrast between the smooth title and the cool, electronic sound. Can you hear how little it resembles jazz or funk?

artiest/thundercat.text: Stephen Bruner, better known as Thundercat, grew up in Los Angeles in a musical family; his brother Ronald Bruner Jr. is a drummer. As a teenager he played in the punk band Suicidal Tendencies. He plays a six-string bass guitar and names Jaco Pastorius as a major influence. He worked closely with the producer Flying Lotus and played on Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp a Butterfly, for which he received a Grammy. On his own albums such as Drunk (2017), he sings funny and melancholy songs in a high voice over virtuosic bass lines. For It Is What It Is (2020) he received a Grammy.
artiest/thundercat.listen: Listen to the bass, which plays chords and melodies beneath the soft vocals.

artiest/tiesto.text:
Tiësto is the stage name of Tijs Verwest, born in Breda in 1969. As a teenager he listened to the radio shows of Ferry Maat and Ben Liebrand, and at fourteen he was already DJing at school parties. In the 1980s and early 1990s he was a DJ in clubs in Breda and the surrounding area, at first playing new beat and acid house. From 1994 he also made his own records, at first hardcore and gabber under other names. In 1997 he started the label Black Hole Recordings with Arny Bink, on which his mix series Magik and In Search of Sunrise appeared.

With Ferry Corsten he made trance as Gouryella, and he worked on other projects with Armin van Buuren. His remix of Silence by Delerium brought him to a large audience around 2000. In 2001 came his first solo album, In My Memory, and from 2002 to 2004 he was voted the world's best DJ three years in a row. In 2003 he became the first DJ to give a solo concert in a packed GelreDome, where he opened with his version of Adagio for Strings. That piece became the starting point for his music at the opening of the 2004 Olympic Games in Athens, where he was the first DJ to perform live. Among the albums that followed were Just Be (2004), Elements of Life (2007) and Kaleidoscope (2009).

Tiësto made trance big: long build-ups, floating synthesizer sounds and euphoric peaks, made for enormous halls. He showed that a DJ could fill a stadium single-handedly. In doing so he became one of the Dutch DJs who made electronic dance music known around the world.
artiest/tiesto.listen: Listen to Adagio for Strings and notice how Tiësto turns a well-known classical piece by Samuel Barber into dance music. Hear how the melody first sounds softly and how the beat then comes in and builds the tension towards a peak.

artiest/tigran-hamasyan.text: The pianist Tigran Hamasyan was born in Gyumri, Armenia, and moved to Los Angeles with his family as a teenager. In 2006 he won the prestigious Thelonious Monk piano competition. In his music he combines Armenian folk songs and church music with jazz, electronics and the heavy, complex rhythms of progressive metal. On A Fable (2011) he plays solo; on Mockroot (2015) with bass and drums. He also sometimes sings along wordlessly with his piano. He performs a lot in Europe, including in the Netherlands.
artiest/tigran-hamasyan.listen: Count along: the rhythm keeps changing in length.

artiest/tim-rice.text:
Sir Timothy Miles Bindon Rice, born in 1944, is an English lyricist. He was born at a country house near Amersham, briefly trained at a law firm in London and studied for a year at the Sorbonne. In 1966 he started at EMI Records, and in 1968 he became an assistant to the producer Norrie Paramor, where he worked with Cliff Richard and the Scaffold, among others. He then made his name in musical theatre, above all with Andrew Lloyd Webber. Together they wrote Joseph and the Amazing Technicolor Dreamcoat, Jesus Christ Superstar and Evita. Joseph and Superstar were among the first hit musicals to draw their sound from the rock and pop of the 1960s.

He also worked successfully with others. With Björn Ulvaeus and Benny Andersson of ABBA he wrote Chess, which includes the British number one I Know Him So Well. For Disney he wrote the songs for Aladdin with Alan Menken, for which A Whole New World won an Oscar, a Golden Globe and a Grammy in 1992, as well as the stage version of Beauty and the Beast. With Elton John he made The Lion King, with Can You Feel the Love Tonight, and Aida. For the film version of Evita he received a third Oscar in 1996, for You Must Love Me.

Rice is one of twenty-eight people who have won an Emmy, an Oscar, a Grammy and a Tony. He was knighted in 1994 and entered the Songwriters Hall of Fame in 1999. He mainly writes lyrics, that is the story and the phrases, and leaves the melody to his composers. He is also known as a radio panellist and cricket enthusiast, and was a co-founder of the Guinness Book of British Hit Singles.
artiest/tim-rice.listen: Listen to I Know Him So Well from Chess and notice how the two female singers carry the lyrics, in turn and together. Can you hear how the words tell a story of love and rivalry?

artiest/timbaland.text:
Timbaland, in full Timothy Zachery Mosley, is an American producer, rapper, singer and songwriter. He was born in 1972 in Norfolk, Virginia. Already at secondary school he worked with the rapper Magoo and was part of the production group S.B.I., which also included his cousin Pharrell Williams. At fourteen he was accidentally shot and lay partially paralysed for months. During that time he taught himself to DJ with his left hand. Through Magoo, Missy Elliott heard his material. The producer DeVante Swing brought them to New York and gave him the name Timbaland, after the Timberland boot.

His first major production was Ginuwine... the Bachelor in 1996. Aaliyah's One in a Million followed in 1996 and Missy Elliott's Supa Dupa Fly in 1997. Together with Elliott he made, from 1997, the albums that established her name. As an artist himself he released Tim's Bio in 1998, among others, alongside three albums as Timbaland and Magoo. In 2002 he produced Cry Me a River for Justin Timberlake, and later also most of his albums, including FutureSex/LoveSounds. In 2007 came his own album Shock Value, with Give It to Me, The Way I Are and Apologize with OneRepublic. He also made music for Michael Jackson, Jay-Z, Beyoncé, Madonna and Rihanna, and founded labels such as Beat Club and Mosley Music Group.

His trademark is a hesitating, stuttering rhythm with which he makes a beat stumble for a moment, again and again. Entertainment Weekly wrote in 2007 that almost every pop trend of the moment could be traced back to him, from tough R&B singers to the use of avant-garde sounds in songs that were number one.
artiest/timbaland.listen: Listen to Cry Me a River by Justin Timberlake, produced by Timbaland. Notice the rhythm that seems to falter for a moment again and again, and the dark, sparse sounds beneath the vocals.

artiest/timmy-thomas.text:
Timothy Earle Thomas was born in 1944 in Evansville, Indiana, one of twelve children of a Methodist minister, and died in 2022. His father taught all the children to play piano. He studied at Lane College in Tennessee, accompanied Donald Byrd and Cannonball Adderley and worked as a session musician in Memphis. In the 1960s he released singles on Goldwax Records, among them Have Some Boogaloo and It's My Life. He then moved to Miami, where in 1972 he opened a café of his own and signed with Glades Records.

In 1972 he wrote and recorded Why Can't We Live Together, inspired by hatred, racism and the Vietnam War. The song is stripped down: Thomas plays organ himself, accompanied by a drum machine. The record topped Billboard's R&B chart, reached number three on the Hot 100 and number twelve in Britain, and sold more than two million copies. People Are Changin' followed in 1973, the album You're the Song I've Always Wanted to Sing in 1974, and The Magician in 1976. In 1984 he reached the American soul chart with Gotta Give a Little Love (Ten Years After). In the 1990s he worked as a producer, and his song Dying Inside to Hold You became popular in the Philippines.

The influence of his big hit remains remarkable. In 2015 Drake sampled it in Hotline Bling, and the bare sound of drum machine and organ is regarded as an early forerunner of later soul and hip-hop.
artiest/timmy-thomas.listen: Listen to Why Can't We Live Together and notice the simple drum machine and the organ, with which the singer conveys an urgent message using very few means. Can you hear how the space in the song emphasises the voice?

artiest/tina-guo.text:
Tina Guo was born in Shanghai in 1985 and is a Chinese-American cellist and erhu player from San Diego. Her father was a concert cellist and her mother a concert violinist. She began piano at the age of three, moved with her family to the United States at five and received violin lessons there from her mother. Later she took up the cello. She has appeared as a soloist with symphony orchestras in San Diego, Greece and Brazil, among other places.

Her first solo album was Autumn Winds in 2009, a classical new age record. Others followed, including The Journey, Eternity, Cello Metal in 2015, Game On! in 2017 and Dies Irae in 2021. She plays both acoustic and electric cello. Her videos stand out for their theatrical sets and exuberant costumes, and she combines genres. From 2011 to 2013 she toured as electric cellist with Cirque du Soleil's Michael Jackson: The Immortal World Tour. She also played with the Foo Fighters at the Grammy Awards and with Hans Zimmer.

Guo has played the cello in the music of many films, series and computer games, including Sherlock Holmes, Iron Man 2 and Diablo III, and above all the Wonder Woman theme in Batman v Superman, together with Zimmer. This has made her a familiar face of film music and game music. She has also played with metal bands such as Sabaton, and released a sample library that many composers use.
artiest/tina-guo.listen: Listen to the Wonder Woman theme on electric cello and notice the raw, almost guitar-like sound of the instrument. Can you hear how the cello takes the place of a rock guitar here?

artiest/tina-turner.text:
Tina Turner was born Anna Mae Bullock in 1939 in Brownsville, Tennessee, and died in 2023 in Switzerland. As a child she sang in the church choir, and in 1956 she moved to St. Louis. There she met Ike Turner and his band, the Kings of Rhythm. One evening she picked up the microphone and sang a song by B.B. King, after which Ike made her the group's singer. He gave her the name Tina. In 1960 A Fool in Love came out, the first record by Ike and Tina Turner. The Ike and Tina Turner Revue, with the Ikettes as backing singers and dancers, became famous for its explosive performances.

In 1966 Phil Spector produced River Deep, Mountain High, which reached number three in Britain and flopped in the United States. It earned the group a place as support act to the Rolling Stones. In 1971 Proud Mary, a cover of a song by Creedence Clearwater Revival, became their biggest hit, and Nutbush City Limits followed. In 1976 Tina left Ike and began a solo career. With Let's Stay Together in 1983 and above all the album Private Dancer in 1984 she made a major comeback. What's Love Got to Do with It won the Grammy for Record of the Year in 1985 and became her only number one on the Billboard Hot 100.

Turner also sang Better Be Good to Me, We Don't Need Another Hero and the title song of the Bond film GoldenEye. She acted in films such as Tommy and Mad Max Beyond Thunderdome. With her powerful voice and energetic stage presence she broke down barriers in rock music, and she is called the Queen of Rock 'n' Roll.
artiest/tina-turner.listen: Listen to Proud Mary by Ike and Tina Turner and notice the calm beginning and the switch to a frenzied tempo. Can you hear how Tina's voice becomes rougher and wilder as the song moves on?

artiest/tina-weymouth.text:
Tina Weymouth, in full Martina Michèle Weymouth, is an American bassist, singer and songwriter. She was born in 1950 in Coronado, California, the daughter of an American naval officer and a French mother from Brittany. Because of her father's career the family moved often, to Hawaii, France, Belgium, Switzerland and Iceland, among other places. At twelve she played in a handbell ensemble, and at fourteen she taught herself guitar. At the Rhode Island School of Design she met Chris Frantz and David Byrne, who formed the band Talking Heads.

She began as Frantz's girlfriend and the group's driver. When Byrne and Frantz could not find a suitable bassist, Frantz asked her to learn the instrument. After she graduated the three moved to New York. Weymouth combined the sober art punk bass lines of groups such as Wire and Pere Ubu with danceable, funky riffs, and so formed the basis of the Talking Heads sound. In 1980 she founded Tom Tom Club with Frantz, a side project that kept them occupied during a long break of the band. In 1996 Weymouth, Frantz and Jerry Harrison released the album No Talking, Just Head under the name The Heads, without Byrne. In 1992 she co-produced Yes Please! by Happy Mondays and sang on 19-2000 by Gorillaz.

In 2002 she was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame with Talking Heads. Her bass lines are bare and carefully considered: a few notes that are exactly enough. That her playing in Psycho Killer revolves around a single note and so carries all the tension shows that a bassist can be the core of a song. With it she showed that melody and rhythm can lie close together in a bass player.
artiest/tina-weymouth.listen: Listen to Psycho Killer by Talking Heads. Notice the bare bass line of Tina Weymouth that carries the song, and the French passage in the lyrics.

artiest/tito-puente.text:
Tito Puente, born Ernest Anthony Puente in Harlem, New York, in 1923, grew up in Spanish Harlem as the son of Puerto Rican parents. As a seven-year-old boy he drummed on pots and window frames, after which his mother had him take piano lessons. At ten he chose percussion, inspired by the drummer Gene Krupa. He wanted to dance, but an ankle injury put an end to that. At sixteen he played in Ramon Oliver's band and then in Machito's orchestra, where he replaced a drummer who had been called up.

After his service in the navy he studied conducting and orchestration at the Juilliard School. His teacher was Japanese, and Asian influences can be heard in his compositions and arrangements. Puente was a bandleader, percussionist on the timbales, vibraphonist and producer. He made dance music in mambo and Latin jazz and was called El Rey de los Timbales. Albums such as Mambo Caravan from 1956, Dance Mania from 1958 and Top Percussion from 1958 preserve that work. His music can be heard in films such as The Mambo Kings and Calle 54, and he also appeared in television programmes such as Sesame Street and The Simpsons.

Puente joined the Afro-Cuban sound of the mambo to the power of big band jazz. He died in 2000. Oye Como Va from 1963 and Ran Kan Kan from 1949 show how danceable that combination was.
artiest/tito-puente.listen: Listen to Oye Como Va by Tito Puente. Notice the timbales, the tight rhythm and the short brass accents that drive the dance.

artiest/tito-rodriguez.text:
Pablo Rodríguez Lozada, better known as Tito Rodríguez, was born in 1923 in Santurce, Puerto Rico, and died in 1973. He was a singer and bandleader. At thirteen he was already singing in a group, and in 1940 he moved to New York, where his brother Johnny, also a singer and composer, was already living. He worked as a singer and bongo player for orchestras including those of Eric Madriguera and Xavier Cugat, served a year in the American army and afterwards played with José Curbelo.

In 1947 he founded his own orchestra, Los Diablos del Mambo, later Los Lobos del Mambo and finally The Tito Rodríguez Orchestra. His best years were the 1950s, at the height of the craze for mambo and cha-cha-cha. He also recorded boleros, sones, guarachas and pachangas. In New York he was the great rival of Tito Puente, a friendly rivalry that became an urban legend. He discovered Cheo Feliciano, and performed at the Palladium Ballroom alongside the orchestras of Machito, Tito Puente and Charlie Palmieri.

At United Artists he devoted himself to boleros. Inolvidable, a bolero by the Cuban composer Julio Gutiérrez, sold one and a half million copies in 1963 and gave him the nickname El Inolvidable. He performed at Birdland with jazz musicians such as Bob Brookmeyer, Al Cohn, Zoot Sims and Clark Terry. In 1966 he returned to Puerto Rico, where he started a television show and a label of his own. In 1999 he was inducted into the International Latin Music Hall of Fame.
artiest/tito-rodriguez.listen: Listen to Inolvidable and notice the soft, smooth voice above the calm bolero rhythm. Can you hear how gently and intimately he sings, compared with the dance numbers from his mambo years?

artiest/tj-koleoso.text:
TJ Koleoso is the bassist of the British jazz group Ezra Collective. The group formed in 2012 in London around the brothers Femi Koleoso on drums and TJ Koleoso on electric bass, together with the saxophonist James Mollison, the keyboardist Joe Armon-Jones and the trumpeter Dylan Jones, later replaced by Ife Ogunjobi. The members met on the jazz programme Tomorrow's Warriors for young musicians. The name refers to the prophet Ezra, who studied the works of great predecessors, something the group also wanted to do in jazz.

The group's music blends Afrobeat, calypso, reggae, hip-hop, soul and jazz. The debut album You Can't Steal My Joy appeared in 2019, with guests such as Jorja Smith and Loyle Carner. In 2022 came Where I'm Meant to Be, which won the Mercury Prize in 2023, the first time a jazz group received that prize. The 2024 song God Gave Me Feet for Dancing was on Barack Obama's list of favourite songs. In 2025 the group won the Brit Award for Group of the Year, also as the first jazz band.

The group names Robert Glasper and Kendrick Lamar's To Pimp a Butterfly as early inspirations, and often plays with other London jazz musicians, such as Nubya Garcia and Moses Boyd. In that group, TJ Koleoso's bass carries the groove, alongside his brother's drums.
artiest/tj-koleoso.listen: Listen to God Gave Me Feet for Dancing by Ezra Collective and notice the bass line that, together with the drums, holds the groove in place. Can you hear how jazz is joined here with dance music?

artiest/tlc.text:
TLC is an American girl group from Atlanta, formed in 1990. The best-known line-up consisted of Tionne Watkins (T-Boz), Lisa Lopes (Left Eye) and Rozonda Thomas (Chilli). The name was an abbreviation of the first names of the original members. The singer Pebbles became their manager and brought them to L.A. Reid and Babyface's label LaFace. In 1991 Chilli joined, and the nicknames were chosen so that the letters TLC still fitted.

The debut Ooooooohhh... On the TLC Tip (1992) was a mix of funk, hip-hop and R&B, in the style of new jack swing. Watkins sang low, Thomas higher and Lopes rapped. With their bright clothing and playful, self-assured lyrics they stood out at once. The second album CrazySexyCool (1994) sounded more mature and smoother, with deep grooves and hip-hop beats. Creep and Waterfalls became number one hits. Waterfalls, with a soulful arrangement and a personal rap by Lopes, warned against drug dealing and unsafe sex and became their biggest hit. On FanMail (1999) came No Scrubs and Unpretty.

Behind the scenes things often went wrong. The group earned little from its success, Watkins suffered from sickle cell disease and Lopes struggled with alcohol. In 2002 Lopes was killed in a car accident in Honduras. Watkins and Thomas carried on as a duo. TLC is one of the best-selling American girl groups and paved the way for groups such as Destiny's Child.
artiest/tlc.listen: Listen to Waterfalls from 1994. Notice the warm soul sound with horns, T-Boz's calm singing, and how Left Eye's rap gives the song a personal turn halfway through.

artiest/toby-fox.text: Toby Fox was born in 1991 in Manchester, New Hampshire. He taught himself to compose and from 2010 contributed to the music of the webcomic Homestuck. He made his game Undertale (2015) almost on his own, with the artist Temmie Chang. He raised the money through Kickstarter. He made all the music in the program FL Studio. As an important influence he names the Japanese Mother series, especially EarthBound. The score is known for its leitmotifs: characters' themes keep returning, and in 'Hopes and Dreams' almost all of them sound. He had already used 'Megalovania' earlier in Homestuck and in a self-made modification of EarthBound. Since 2018 the sequel Deltarune has been appearing in chapters.
artiest/toby-fox.listen: Notice the leitmotifs: short melodies that return at a different tempo or in a different tone colour, and the sound of old game consoles alongside modern electronics.

artiest/tokyo-metropolitan-symphony-orch.text:
The Tokyo Metropolitan Symphony Orchestra, known in Japan simply as Tokyō, is a Japanese symphony orchestra in Tokyo. The city of Tokyo founded the orchestra in 1965, in the wake of the 1964 Olympic Games. Heinz Hofmann was the first permanent conductor, from 1965 to 1967. The orchestra regularly plays at the Tokyo Bunka Kaikan, which also houses its offices, at Suntory Hall and at the Tokyo Metropolitan Theatre.

Thanks to the work of Hiroshi Wakasugi, Eliahu Inbal and Gary Bertini, among others, the orchestra regularly plays symphonies by Gustav Mahler. Later music directors included James DePreist and Kazushi Ōno, who has led this orchestra since 2015 and ends his tenure in 2026. Alan Gilbert has been principal guest conductor since 2018, and the Finn Pekka Kuusisto has been announced as chief conductor from 2028. The orchestra won the Kyoto Music Award in 1991, and received Record Academy Awards for recordings under Inbal, including with Shostakovich and with a new Mahler cycle.

The list of recordings is wide. It includes classical works by Bartók, Bizet, Sibelius and Mendelssohn, and Japanese contemporary composers. It also includes symphonic suites from the computer game series Dragon Quest, released between 2004 and 2006. In this way the orchestra builds a bridge between the concert hall and the music of video games, which in Japan has an orchestral audience of its own.
artiest/tokyo-metropolitan-symphony-orch.listen: Listen to a movement from one of the Dragon Quest suites by this orchestra and notice how a melody from a computer game sounds with strings, brass and percussion. Can you hear how the music is developed like an ordinary symphony?

artiest/tom-dissevelt.text:
Tom Dissevelt, in full Thomas Dissevelt, was a Dutch composer, arranger and musician. He was born in 1921 and between 1939 and 1944 studied at the Royal Conservatoire in The Hague, first trombone, then clarinet, music theory and piano. Later he learned double bass with Herman Stotijn of the Residentie Orchestra. After the war he worked in Indonesia and made a three-year tour taking in Spain and North Africa, among other places. In 1955 he became bassist and arranger of the Skymasters. In 1946 he married Rina Reys, the sister of the jazz singer Rita Reys, and also contributed to recordings of hers.

The work that made him famous came about in 1958, when, on the advice of Philips, he was invited to the electronic music studio of the Physics Laboratory in Eindhoven. There he worked with Dick Raaijmakers, a Philips engineer who recorded under the name Kid Baltan. They made music with test oscillators, tapes, filters and reverberation chambers, and cut and stacked tape into pieces that united jazz rhythms with laboratory electronics. This became one of the first European attempts to combine electronic sound with a structured pop form. In 1958 their single Song of the Second Moon appeared. In 1959 the EP Electronic Movements followed, then The Fascinating World of Electronic Music. His solo album Fantasy in Orbit from 1964 was more melodic and spacious. In 2003 David Bowie counted The Fascinating World of Electronic Music among his twenty-five favourite albums.

Because pop music was rising and radio orchestras were being disbanded, in 1965 Dissevelt went to work with Wim Sonneveld as a bassist. He died in 1989. His work was far ahead of its time: it showed the public what new technology could do with music.
artiest/tom-dissevelt.listen: Listen to Song of the Second Moon by Tom Dissevelt and Kid Baltan. Notice the electronic sounds that come straight from a laboratory, and how a regular rhythm holds them together as music.

artiest/tom-dissevelt-en-kid-baltan.text:
Tom Dissevelt was a Dutch composer, arranger and musician, born in 1921 and died in 1989. He was regarded as a pioneer in bringing electronic music and jazz together. Between 1939 and 1944 he studied at the Royal Conservatoire in The Hague, first trombone, then clarinet, music theory and piano, and later double bass. After the war he worked in Indonesia and made a long tour taking in Spain and North Africa, among other places. In 1955 the orchestra of the Skymasters hired him as bassist and arranger. He became interested in twelve-tone music and listened to Karlheinz Stockhausen and Anton Webern.

On the advice of Philips he was invited to work in the electronic studio of the laboratory in Eindhoven, the NatLab. There he worked with Dick Raaijmakers, who made records under the pseudonym Kid Baltan. They composed and recorded with test oscillators, tone generators, tape recorders, filters and reverberation chambers, and cut and spliced tape. This produced pieces in which rhythms from jazz meet laboratory electronics. Their experiments are regarded as one of the first European attempts to combine electronic sound with pop music in a fixed form. Their work has been collected on Popular Electronics, from 2004.

In this way Dissevelt and Baltan wrote a chapter in the history of electronic pop music, long before the synthesizer became commonplace. Song of the Second Moon is an example of that early sound.
artiest/tom-dissevelt-en-kid-baltan.listen: Listen to Song of the Second Moon and notice the pulsing and whooshing sounds. Can you hear how those electronic sounds work almost like a rhythm section?

artiest/tom-jones.text:
Sir Thomas John Woodward, known as Tom Jones, was born in 1940 in Treforest, Wales, the son of a miner. He sang from an early age at family parties and in the school choir, and at the age of twelve spent two years in bed with tuberculosis. In 1963 he became the frontman of the Welsh beat group Tommy Scott and the Senators. The manager Gordon Mills took him to London, named him Tom Jones after the popular 1963 film, and arranged a contract with Decca. His second single, It's Not Unusual, became a number one in Britain in early 1965 and reached the American top ten, partly thanks to the support of the pirate station Radio Caroline.

The following year brought film themes, including for the Bond film Thunderball and What's New Pussycat? by Burt Bacharach and Hal David. In 1966 Jones received a Grammy for Best New Artist. He then grew into a crooner with Green, Green Grass of Home, Delilah and She's a Lady. From 1967 he performed in Las Vegas, in open-necked shirts and tight trousers, and from 1969 to 1971 he had the TV show This Is Tom Jones. His voice is described as a full, robust baritone, with a range that ran from soul to pop crooner.

In the 1980s he did country, and in 1988 he had a hit with a cover of Prince's Kiss, together with Art of Noise. With the 1999 album Reload, full of duets, he reached the top again, and Sex Bomb became one of his biggest singles. In 2006 he was knighted.
artiest/tom-jones.listen: Listen to It's Not Unusual and notice the powerful, full voice above the driving drums and horns. Can you hear how that baritone effortlessly rises above the band?

artiest/tom-lehrer.text:
Tom Lehrer, in full Thomas Andrew Lehrer, was an American musician and mathematician. He was born in 1928 in New York and died in 2025. As a child he loved logic puzzles and mathematics, took piano lessons and was already writing songs in the manner of Broadway at a young age. He was regarded as a child prodigy and began at Harvard at fifteen. There he studied mathematics and wrote funny songs for his friends. In 1951 and 1952 he performed with The Physical Revue for the physics department. Later he taught at MIT, Harvard and the University of California, Santa Cruz, among others.

His first album, Songs by Tom Lehrer, appeared in 1953. In 1959 More of Tom Lehrer followed, which also appeared in a live-recorded version. His songs parodied well-known musical forms, often with melodies of his own. In the early years they revolved around black humour, as in Poisoning Pigeons in the Park, a cheerful waltz about poisoning pigeons. In the 1960s he wrote topical songs for the American version of the satirical television programme That Was the Week That Was, about education, the Second Vatican Council and pollution, among other things. A friend explained to him: always predict the worst, then you will be praised as a prophet. In the early 1970s he largely withdrew from the stage to teach mathematics and the history of musical theatre.

Lehrer showed that a funny song can contain a sharp social message. He sang with a light, cheerful sound, accompanied himself on piano and let the lyrics do the work. In this way he could make a cheerful song even about a subject like the atom bomb, with venom beneath the joke.
artiest/tom-lehrer.listen: Listen to Poisoning Pigeons in the Park by Tom Lehrer. Notice the contrast between the cheerful waltz on piano and the dark lyrics.

artiest/tom-morello.text:
Thomas Baptist Morello was born in 1964 in Harlem, New York, and grew up in Libertyville, Illinois. His father was Kenyan and his mother an American teacher. Already at secondary school he became interested in music and politics, called himself the only anarchist at a conservative school and graduated from Harvard in 1986. He then moved to Los Angeles, played in the band Lock Up and in 1991 formed Rage Against the Machine with the rapper Zack de la Rocha. They signed with Epic in 1992 and made the self-titled debut, followed by Evil Empire, The Battle of Los Angeles and Renegades.

After Rage broke up in 2000 he founded Audioslave with the remaining members and the singer Chris Cornell, which made three albums. He also writes folk under the name The Nightwatchman, and made work with Street Sweeper Social Club and Prophets of Rage. He also plays regularly with Bruce Springsteen. His solo albums include The Atlas Underground in 2018. He co-founded Axis of Justice.

Morello is known for his guitar playing, in which feedback, unusual picking, tapping and many effects define the sound. He names influences such as Black Sabbath, Led Zeppelin, Randy Rhoads, Eddie Van Halen and Run-D.M.C. He combines metal and hip-hop with an outspoken left-wing political conviction. Rolling Stone ranked him eighteenth among the greatest guitarists, and with Rage he was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame in 2023.
artiest/tom-morello.listen: Listen to Killing in the Name by Rage Against the Machine and notice the heavy riff and the guitar solo, in which Morello uses effects to make an almost DJ-like sound. Can you hear how the guitar sounds like a turntable?

artiest/tom-petty-and-the-heartbreakers.text:
Tom Petty and the Heartbreakers was an American rock band from Gainesville, Florida, formed in 1976. The original line-up consisted of singer and rhythm guitarist Tom Petty, lead guitarist Mike Campbell, keyboardist Benmont Tench, drummer Stan Lynch and bassist Ron Blair. Petty had previously played in Mudcrutch and was attached to Shelter Records as a songwriter. In 1982 Blair left the group and Howie Epstein joined. In 1994 Steve Ferrone took Lynch's place.

The band released its first album in 1976, with Breakdown and American Girl. You're Gonna Get It! followed in 1978, Damn the Torpedoes in 1979 with Refugee, Hard Promises in 1981 with The Waiting, Long After Dark in 1982 and Southern Accents in 1985. Later came Learning to Fly in 1991 and Mary Jane's Last Dance in 1993. In 1989 Petty made the solo album Full Moon Fever. In 2002 the band was inducted into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame. The last studio album, Hypnotic Eye, appeared in 2014. After Petty's death in 2017 the band ceased to exist.

Petty wanted to call his music simply rock 'n' roll. Critics speak of southern rock and heartland rock, alongside Bruce Springsteen, Bob Seger and John Mellencamp. The band played clear, melodic rock with guitars and keyboards, and made songs that stayed on the radio for a long time. In this way it became a fixture of American rock.
artiest/tom-petty-and-the-heartbreakers.listen: Listen to American Girl and notice the guitar sound and the driving drums. Can you hear how the song keeps pushing forward without becoming heavy?

artiest/tom-turpin.text:
Thomas Million John Turpin was an American composer of ragtime. He was born around 1871 in Savannah, Georgia, and died in 1922 of peritonitis. His exact year of birth is uncertain, since both 1871 and 1873 appear in sources, and his gravestone says 1871. At a young age he opened a saloon in St. Louis, the Rosebud Café, which became a meeting place for local pianists, among them Joe Jordan and Scott Joplin. Joplin's Rosebud March from 1905 is named after the café. The saloon closed in 1906.

Turpin is regarded as the composer of the first published rag by an African American: Harlem Rag from 1897, although according to the source the piece had already been composed in 1892, a year before the 1893 World's Fair, where ragtime found its first large audience. In total he published seven compositions. Two were recorded at the time: St. Louis Rag from 1903, by the United States Marine Band and by Arthur Pryor's orchestra in 1906, among others, and Buffalo Rag from 1904, by Vess L. Ossman.

Turpin was a big man, and his piano stood on blocks so that he could play standing up. Besides the café he ran a theatre, gambling houses and dance halls together with his brother Charles, and he was a deputy constable, one of the first politically powerful African Americans in St. Louis. His influence on local music earned him the title Father of St. Louis Ragtime.
artiest/tom-turpin.listen: Listen to Harlem Rag on piano and notice the left hand, which plays a regular, marching bass while the right hand lays syncopations over it. Can you hear how that displacement gives ragtime its own swing?

artiest/tomas-luis-de-victoria.text:
Tomás Luis de Victoria was born around 1548, probably in Ávila, and died in 1611 in Madrid. He is regarded as the most famous Spanish composer of the Renaissance and stands beside Palestrina and Orlande de Lassus as one of the most important composers of the late Renaissance. His father died in 1557, and his uncle, a priest, became his guardian. He was a choirboy at Ávila Cathedral. With an allowance from Philip II he went to Rome in 1565, where he became a singer at the Collegium Germanicum and possibly studied with Palestrina. In 1574 he was ordained a priest. In 1587 he returned to Spain, as chaplain to the Empress María at the Descalzas Reales convent in Madrid, where he later became organist.

His surviving work consists almost entirely of sacred, polyphonic vocal music on Latin texts: masses, motets, antiphons and responsories. In 1572 his first book of motets appeared, and in 1585 the Officium Hebdomadae Sanctae, which includes the Tenebrae Responsories for Holy Week. His masterpiece is the Officium Defunctorum from 1605, a requiem for the Empress María. He also wrote for more than one choir, following the example of the Venetian school.

Victoria shuns the intricate counterpoint of many of his contemporaries and chooses simple lines and homophonic textures, with strong rhythmic contrasts and sometimes pictorial word-setting as in a madrigal. His melodies and dissonances are freer than Palestrina's. Many listeners hear a mystical intensity and direct emotion in his music. His work enjoyed a revival in the twentieth century, with many recordings, including by The Tallis Scholars.
artiest/tomas-luis-de-victoria.listen: Listen to a movement from the Requiem Officium Defunctorum and notice the soft, calm singing in which the text is carried by the choir almost like a spoken word. Can you hear how the intensity increases without the volume ever becoming really loud?

artiest/tomasz-stanko.text: The trumpeter Tomasz Stańko was born in 1942 in Rzeszów. In 1962 he founded the group Jazz Darings with the pianist Adam Makowicz, inspired by the free jazz of Ornette Coleman. From 1963 to 1967 he played in Krzysztof Komeda's quintet, including on Astigmatic. Miles Davis was also an important example. For ECM he recorded Balladyna in 1975, with the bassist Dave Holland, and in 1997 Litania, a tribute to Komeda. For Soul of Things (recorded in 2001) he chose the young trio of the pianist Marcin Wasilewski. His tone is dark and hoarse, with long pauses. He died in Warsaw in 2018.
artiest/tomasz-stanko.listen: Hear the dark, hoarse trumpet tone and the silences between the phrases.

artiest/tomasz-szukalski.text:
Tomasz Szukalski was born in 1947 in Warsaw and died in 2012 in Piaseczno, Poland. He was a Polish jazz saxophonist, composer and improviser. He studied clarinet, but preferred to play tenor and soprano saxophone, and sometimes bass or baritone saxophone. His playing was often compared with that of John Coltrane and Ben Webster. He graduated from the Chopin University of Music in Warsaw. His career began in the jazz orchestras of Zbigniew Namysłowski and Jan Ptaszyn Wróblewski, alongside Tomasz Stańko and Michał Urbaniak, among others.

In the 1970s his playing became freer and more avant-garde. He worked with Stańko and with Scandinavian musicians such as Edward Vesala, Arild Andersen and Terje Rypdal. In 1975 he played on Stańko's album Balladyna for ECM, and in Poland he performed with the rock group SBB. In 1977 he founded his own group The Quartet, which gained a great reputation. With SBB's leader Józef Skrzek he made the album Ambitus Extended. During martial law he played with Wróblewski again. In 1984 he recorded Time Killers with Wojciech Karolak and Czesław Bartkowski, a record that was an instant hit.

After 1990 he often worked with the young pianist Artur Dutkiewicz and performed in changing line-ups. For a long time he lived in a simple hut outside Warsaw. Around 2009 Dutkiewicz organised benefit concerts for him, called The Day of the Jackal. Szukalski is regarded as a celebrated master of the tenor saxophone in Polish jazz.
artiest/tomasz-szukalski.listen: Listen to Time Killers by Tomasz Szukalski and notice the warm, full tone of the tenor saxophone above the loose groove. Can you hear how the saxophone holds on to the melody almost as if singing?

artiest/tommy-bolin.text:
Tommy Bolin was an American guitarist and songwriter who combined rock and jazz rock. He was born in 1951 in Sioux City, Iowa, began playing in bands at thirteen and called himself a guitarist who plays by ear. In 1969 he joined Zephyr in Boulder, Colorado, a band with the singer Candy Givens. In 1972 he founded the fusion project Energy, which released no album during his lifetime.

His name went through the music world when in 1973 he played on drummer Billy Cobham's Spectrum. That same year he became guitarist of the James Gang, with whom he recorded Bang (1973) and Miami (1974). Deep Purple's keyboardist Jon Lord later said that Spectrum convinced him to carry on after Ritchie Blackmore's departure after all. So Bolin ended up in Deep Purple in 1975, where he wrote or co-wrote the majority of Come Taste the Band, including the instrumental Owed to G, a tribute to George Gershwin. His first solo album Teaser appeared in November 1975, the second, Private Eyes, in 1976.

Bolin played with a loose, melodic approach that fitted both hard rock and jazz fusion. Many Deep Purple fans expected a clone of Blackmore, but his style was very different. Drug problems marked his last years. On 4 December 1976 he died in Miami of an overdose, straight after a concert as the opening act for Jeff Beck. He was 25 years old. Later tributes and posthumously released recordings keep his work alive.
artiest/tommy-bolin.listen: Listen to Spectrum by Billy Cobham, where Bolin plays guitar on four tracks, and notice how a rock guitarist feels at home among jazz drums and synthesizers.

artiest/tommy-dorsey.text:
Tommy Dorsey was an American trombonist, composer and bandleader from the big band era. He was born in 1905 in Mahanoy Plane, Pennsylvania, and first learned trumpet from his father before switching to trombone. Together with his older brother Jimmy he played in bands including Paul Whiteman's. As The Dorsey Brothers they had their first hit in 1929 with Coquette. After a quarrel Tommy walked out in 1935 to start an orchestra of his own.

His soft, smooth trombone tone earned him the nickname Sentimental Gentleman of Swing, and his theme song was I'm Getting Sentimental Over You. His orchestra played ballads at danceable tempos and worked with singers such as Jack Leonard and Frank Sinatra. From 1940 to 1942 Sinatra sang eighty recordings with the band and said that he learned breathing by watching Dorsey play. In 1939 Dorsey brought in the arranger Sy Oliver, who brought Opus One and Well, Git It. I'll Never Smile Again spent twelve weeks at number one in 1940. Also well known are On Treasure Island, Marie and This Love of Mine.

The orchestra included Buddy Rich, Bunny Berigan and Charlie Shavers, among others, and arrangers such as Axel Stordahl and Nelson Riddle got their first work here. In 1956 the brothers presented Elvis Presley to the national audience for the first time on their television show Stage Show. Dorsey died in November 1956 at the age of 51.
artiest/tommy-dorsey.listen: Listen to I'll Never Smile Again and notice how Dorsey's trombone almost sings the melody while the singer works around it.

artiest/tommy-dorsey-and-his-orchestra.text:
Tommy Dorsey and His Orchestra was the big band that the trombonist Tommy Dorsey founded in 1935, after leaving the joint orchestra with his brother Jimmy. It soon did well: after the move to RCA Victor four hits followed in 1935, with On Treasure Island as the first. The orchestra was known for ballads at a danceable tempo, played around the leader's soft trombone.

When critics felt in 1939 that the jazz feeling was missing, Dorsey lured the arranger Sy Oliver away from Jimmie Lunceford's orchestra. Oliver wrote Opus One and Well, Git It, among others. The band also had the small group Clambake Seven, which played Dixieland during performances. The orchestra let young singers break through, among them Jack Leonard, Jo Stafford with the Pied Pipers and above all Frank Sinatra, who from 1940 to 1942 made eighty recordings with the band, including This Love of Mine. The instrumentalists were of a high standard: the drummer Buddy Rich, the trumpeter Bunny Berigan and later Charlie Shavers played in it. Arrangers such as Axel Stordahl, Paul Weston and Nelson Riddle also came from this circle.

Dorsey disbanded the orchestra at the end of 1946, but re-formed it in 1947. After his death in 1956 the band carried on under various leaders: Warren Covington had a hit in 1958 with Tea for Two Cha-Cha, and Sam Donahue and Buddy Morrow followed later. That is why so many later albums still bear the name of the orchestra.
artiest/tommy-dorsey-and-his-orchestra.listen: Listen to Opus One and notice how Sy Oliver's arrangements make the instrument groups, such as trumpets and trombones, answer one another, to the rhythm of a swinging dance band.
